learningObjective: See that InfoNCE asks an anchor to identify one declared positive among all candidates, so positive and negative sampling choices determine both the learned invariance and false-negative pressure.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG candidate map is the smallest medium that can align an anchor, its two-view positive, ordinary negatives, and a nearby false negative with the numerator and denominator of InfoNCE. Fixed geometry makes the data-contract error spatially apparent without simulating training.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: a flowchart can show augmentation and encoding stages but cannot make one positive competing against a spatial candidate set or the nearby false-negative conflict legible.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: fixed coordinates, direct labels, line styles, and shape differences expose which candidate enters the numerator, which candidates enter the denominator, and why a semantically related in-batch item can receive the wrong gradient.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: a table could list positive and negative roles, but would not show that all candidates compete relative to the same anchor or that semantic nearness can disagree with the sampling label.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: a temperature or augmentation control would add state without improving the foundational lesson that candidate construction precedes optimization.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: SimCLR includes a related framework figure and CPC includes contrastive schematics, but reuse permission for paper artwork was not established and neither isolates the false-negative data contract taught here. No source composition is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the prose gives the loss, positive-pair table, and negative-sampling risks in separate sections, leaving the reader to mentally connect the single numerator choice to every denominator competitor.

pages.insight: The preceding classification-loss slide covers softmax and negative log likelihood, providing denominator context but no representation-pair construction.

The loss slide defines anchor, positive, and negative embeddings for triplet loss; it is the deck's closest explicit pairwise-learning treatment, but it is margin-based rather than InfoNCE and does not discuss augmentations or false negatives.
The following slide moves to classification evaluation metrics, ending the local pairwise-loss neighborhood.
The recommender data slide defines user-item interactions and successful search sessions, supplying the interaction context from which positives might be constructed.
The personalized-recommender slide says to train from the user-item matrix with contrastive learning, but gives no objective, positive definition, negative sampling rule, or visual mechanism.

The neighboring content-based recommender slide switches to knowledge-graph triplets and title similarity, confirming that the contrastive treatment is limited to the one-line recommendation on page 138.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page local deck was text-indexed for contrastive, self-supervised, InfoNCE, SimCLR, CLIP, positive pair, negative sampling, and representation learning. Pages 35-37 and 137-139 were then inspected as the full relevant neighborhoods. Page 36 supplies anchor-positive-negative vocabulary for triplet loss, and page 138 only recommends contrastive learning for personalization. The deck contains no InfoNCE candidate-set explanation or self-supervised augmentation visual. No deck artwork, examples, coordinates, wording, or layout is reused.

sources.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
sources.usage: Used as the primary source to verify that two independently augmented views of each example form a positive pair, the other augmented examples in the minibatch act as negatives, and augmentation composition defines the predictive task.
sources.license: The paper is publicly accessible through PMLR, but no explicit permissive license for its figures was identified. The related SimCLR software is Apache-2.0 licensed, which is not treated as permission to reuse paper artwork. No figure, data, result, wording, or layout is copied.

sources.title: Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding
sources.usage: Used as the primary source for InfoNCE as a categorical objective that selects a positive sample from a set containing one positive and multiple negatives.
sources.license: The arXiv record and paper are publicly accessible, but public access is not assumed to grant figure-reuse rights. No source figure, experiment, wording, or layout is reproduced.

sources.title: Debiased Contrastive Learning
sources.usage: Used as the primary source to verify that randomly sampled negatives may actually share the anchor's latent class and therefore create false-negative bias.
sources.license: No source figure, dataset, empirical result, wording, or layout is reused. The paper is cited only for the false-negative mechanism because figure permission was not established.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is the data contract hidden inside the loss: for one anchor, exactly one declared positive occupies the numerator while every candidate in the denominator competes with it. A second view of the same source is intentionally invariant, but an independently sampled item can be semantically valid and still be pushed away as a false negative. The visual is an original schematic using synthetic labels and coordinates, not a reconstruction of any paper figure.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected both exact slide neighborhoods, then reviewed the primary SimCLR, CPC, and debiased contrastive-learning papers before selecting an original InfoNCE candidate-set SVG.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and long description. Direct role labels, distinct circle and diamond shapes, a solid positive connector, dashed negative connectors, and an explicit warning callout carry the full lesson without color. Its 360-pixel viewBox scales to the reading column without a minimum width for readability at 390 CSS pixels; existing theme variables provide dark-mode and print-compatible contrast.
